questions.question: What makes an RNN suitable for sequences?
options: It carries a hidden state and shares weights across time steps
It processes all tokens at once
questions.explanation: The hidden state is the memory; shared weights handle any length.

questions.question: Sentiment classification of a review (sequence in, one label out) is which RNN pattern?
questions.explanation: Many inputs, one output.

questions.question: Image captioning (one image in, a sentence out) is:
questions.explanation: One input, a sequence out.

questions.question: RNNs are trained with:
questions.explanation: BPTT unrolls the network over time steps and backpropagates through them.

questions.question: Why do simple RNNs struggle with long sentences?
options: Vanishing gradients over many time steps
They need labels for every word
questions.explanation: Repeated multiplication shrinks gradients, so early inputs barely affect learning.

questions.question: The standard fix for exploding gradients is:
questions.explanation: Clip the gradient norm to a threshold.

questions.question: Which gates does an LSTM have? (select all)
questions.explanation: The reset gate belongs to the GRU.

questions.question: A GRU differs from an LSTM in that it:
options: Has no separate cell state and fewer parameters
questions.explanation: GRU: update + reset gates, merges cell and hidden state.

questions.question: The LSTM's cell state helps long-range memory because:
options: It is updated additively, letting gradients flow
It removes the need for training
questions.explanation: The additive path (gated by the forget gate) avoids repeated squashing.

questions.question: A SimpleRNN layer has input size 8 and 16 hidden units. Parameters (with bias)?
Same input 8 and hidden 16, but an LSTM. Parameters (one bias per gate)?
In a seq2seq translation model, the encoder's job is to:
options: Compress the source sentence into a context representation
questions.explanation: The decoder then generates from that context.

questions.question: The main weakness of the basic encoder–decoder (no attention) is:
options: The fixed-length context vector is a bottleneck for long inputs
questions.explanation: All information must fit one vector; attention fixes this.

questions.question: Teacher forcing means during training the decoder receives:
questions.explanation: Speeds training; the mismatch with inference is called exposure bias.

questions.question: Beam search with beam width 1 is the same as:
questions.explanation: Keeping only the single best path each step is greedy.

questions.question: Why is a bidirectional RNN unsuitable for generating text left to right?
options: It needs future tokens, which don't exist yet during generation
questions.explanation: The backward pass reads the future — fine for tagging, not for generation.

questions.question: Which tasks are naturally sequential data problems? (select all)
questions.explanation: A single tabular row has no order dimension.

questions.question: Why can't an RNN be fully parallelised over the tokens of a sentence during training?
options: Each hidden state depends on the previous one
questions.explanation: h_t needs h_(t−1). Transformers remove this dependency.

questions.question: Part-of-speech tagging every word of a sentence is which RNN pattern?
questions.explanation: One label per input token.

questions.question: An activation commonly used for the RNN hidden state is:
questions.explanation: tanh keeps values in (−1, 1); gates use sigmoid.

questions.question: LSTM gates use the sigmoid function because:
options: It outputs values between 0 and 1, acting as a soft on/off switch
questions.explanation: 0 = block, 1 = pass through.

questions.question: Encoder–decoder models allow input and output sequences to:
questions.explanation: e.g. a 3-word English sentence → 5-word Hindi sentence.

questions.question: Time-series forecasting of the next day's demand from the past 30 days is a natural fit for:
questions.explanation: Sequential input, predict next value.

questions.question: Beam search improves on greedy decoding by:
options: Keeping several partial hypotheses and choosing the best overall sequence
questions.explanation: A locally best word can lead to a worse sentence; beams keep alternatives.
